newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH LABOUR MARKETS NEED MORE FLEXIBILITY -EVA.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH LABOUR MARKETS NEED MORE FLEXIBILITY -EVA.

text.p: The Finnish labour markets should become more flexible to improve employment prospects and politicians and labour market leaders must have the courage to promote change, the Centre for Finnish Business and Policy Studies (EVA) said in a report on Friday.
"There has not been sufficient courage to tackle production structures and inflexibilities of the labour market," EVA said.

Unemployment was becoming expensive, and public finances would be in much less trouble if the billions spent on joblessness could be used to promote "the dynamics and functioning of society," EVA said.
"Political decision-makers seem to think that unemployment is merely a phenomenon stemming from economic recession which will correct itself as economic growth proceeds...," it said.

Measures used to protect domestic production during the era of the closed economy were no longer valid in Europe's single market. The regulatory thinking marking the European Union did not offer support in global competition, it said.

International companies would locate their production and subsidiaries to countries where they think they can obtain adequate high-calibre labour at a cost that is in proportion to the quality of the work, EVA said.
"Stubbornly clinging to regulation mechanisms, institutions and bargaining systems created in an entirely different society and era ... we Finns risk seeing the foundation of our welfare crumble.
In conditions of freely mobile labour, it would also be impossible in the long run to tax a much higher proportion of national income than in other countries, EVA said.

Amidst economic insecurity, people are focused on retaining social security and jobless benefits which have led to incentive traps, and which were not designed for the situation now prevailing in public debt and joblessness, it said.
"There is no going back to the old ways," it said, calling on government and interest groups to adopt a social-minded spirit of discussion and to show leadership.
"Besides courage to change and the ability to learn new things, we need a new approach to work in Finland ... It could be called entrepreneurship," EVA said.
